parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, universal facility ban, or documented police targeting of trans visitors is shown; the only trans-specific incident, a 2014 bathroom arrest, was dismissed with damages won, and health policy formally guarantees care with a 2018 training handbook and legal-aid infrastructure exists. Same-sex criminalisation, expanded in 2006, is secondary under the rubric and not documented as used against trans people, but state campaigns since 1995 involving detention, beating, killing and rape of homosexuals, censorship harassment, infiltration, and absence of general discrimination/violence protections show documented institutional hostility and thin recourse. Enforcement frequency, border/custody practice and current incidents are undocumented, so silence is not safety; extrapolating from the hostile statutory regime and campaign record keeps the rating in Elevated Risk, above organised trans-targeting tiers but well below acceptance-with-working-protections tiers.
